author: muhammad-qassim
body:
I finished the carousel extraction challenge in both Ruby and Python. This was my first time working with Ruby, so it took a bit longer, but I got both versions working with their own parsing logic and tests.

Each extractor pulls name, extensions (like date), link to the Google search result, and image (either inline thumbnail or base64 if it’s a placeholder)

I tested it using three HTML files van-gogh-paintings.html, leonardo-da-vinci-paintings.html, and raphael-paintings.html

Output matches the expected format including base64 thumbnails where needed.

I was planning to make it more generalized to also support other carousels like books or games, but I capped it at the 4-hour mark.

body:
The resources are only ever presented to the UI as Apps so there is room to simplify the special handling of Identity Center Accounts stored in the URC. The extra machinery needed to convert the `identitycenterv1.Account` into a `types.ResourceWithLabels` is no longer needed and is removed. The `IdentityCenterAccountMatcher` was extended to allow being created from a `types.AppServer` so that RBAC is still enforced appropriately on any `types.AppServer`s that are an IC Account.

The IdentityCenterAccountAssignments were also removed entirely from the unified resource cache because they were never consumed. Additionally the resources were exposed via `ListResources` but never consumed and should be made available in their own distinct `ListIdentityCenterAccountAssignments` and `IdentityCenterAccounts` instead of piggybacking on to `ListResources`.



Depends on https://github.com/gravitational/teleport.e/pull/6542.

author: elliottt
body:
Compute the condensation of the package graph, which we can then use to direct the pipeline. This runs Tarjan's algorithm twice: once for the regular imports of a package and once for the test imports. This yields two SCC IDs for each package: that of its application dependencies and that of its test dependencies. As implemented, the test SCC has an implicit dependency on the SCC of its application code, which allows us to skip all normal imports when computing the test SCCs.

This PR also includes an application of this graph: a function to compute a possible parallel traversal order of the package graph, that respects both import and test_import ordering.

### Motivation
Prework for a package-oriented pipeline.

### Test plan
See the new tests about the structure of the returned traversal in `pkg_autocorrect_tests.cc`.

body: This pull request enhances the logic for determining suitable lenses for displaying HTTP response content in the `getSuitableLenses` function. The main changes focus on improving content type detection, prioritizing relevant lenses, and providing fallback options for better user control. ### Enhancements to lens selection logic: * Added a smarter approach for successful responses (`response.type === "success")` by prioritizing lenses that match the content type and dynamically appending additional lenses (e.g., JSON lens) if the content can be parsed into other formats. * Ensured that the raw lens is always included to allow users to view the raw response, even if no specific matching lenses are found. ### Improvements to fallback behavior: * Included all lenses as a fallback option when no matching lenses are detected, giving users full control over lens selection. Closes #5080

author: agustin58ruiz
body:
## Description
main.tf
before:
data "aws_route53_zone" "this" {
  count = local.create_domain_name && var.create_domain_records ? 1 : 0

  name = coalesce(var.hosted_zone_name, local.stripped_domain_name)
}
now:
data "aws_route53_zone" "this" {
  count = local.create_domain_name && var.create_domain_records ? 1 : 0
  private_zone = var.private_zone
  name = coalesce(var.hosted_zone_name, local.stripped_domain_name)
}

variables.tf
added: 

line 159: variable "private_zone" {
  description = "Whether the hosted zone is private or not"
  type        = bool
  default     = false
}

## Motivation and Context
This is needed when someone wants to create records in a private hosted zone. The private_zone argument is required when looking up private zones using the aws_route53_zone data source. Without this parameter, Terraform cannot find the private zone, even if the zone name matches.

## Breaking Changes
This change introduces a new variable (private_zone) with a default value of false, so it is backward compatible.

However, users must explicitly set private_zone = true when creating records in a private hosted zone. Failing to do so will result in the zone not being found.

## Proposed Changes

I used `pytest.mark.parameterize` annotation to pull the inputs out of some test functions in `test_check.py`.  

Wanting to keep everything clean, I decided to create a general `INPUTS` dictionary. The dictionary's key is the function name, and the corresponding value is the extracted test `_input` list. This makes it easy to add inputs for new tests in the future!

For example:

```
INPUTS = {
    "test_check_no_reporter_output": [["examples/nodes/name.py"]],

}

@pytest.mark.parametrize("input_file", INPUTS["test_check_no_reporter_output"])
def test_check_no_reporter_output(prevent_webbrowser_and_httpserver, input_file: Union[str, list[str]]) -> None:

body:
A case was reported that /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpuX/acpi_cppc/highest_perf
have the same value for all CPUs on an Intel hybrid processor (i7-13650hx).
This should be a bug on the driver's side.

To circumvent such a problem, make more efforts to find a source that can tell
the capacity differences among the cores. If there is no such source, resort
to the max frequency of CPUs to estimate CPU capacity.

This should solve the following issue:
  https://github.com/sched-ext/scx/issues/1893

author: titusneyland
body:
These were the likely culprits:

Transaction Usage: In PostRepository.swift, both toggleLike and addComment are using transactions. While this is good for data consistency, it might be causing issues with the security rules. The transaction is trying to update the entire post document, which might be triggering the security rules differently than expected.


Data Structure: The way we're updating the likes and comments arrays might be causing the security rules to evaluate differently than intended. When using transactions, we're updating the entire post document, which might be why the security rules are being more restrictive.

This PR will try to implement linalg functions for Faer device.

API Breaking Change (user should not feel that):
- updates Faer version to v0.22, seems that v0.20/v0.21 changes handling logic for complex values
- Conversion from/to Faer made simple (but API breaking)
- Matmul made simple (but API breaking), now requires `faer::traits::ComplexField` type (trait impl based), instead of manually dispatch types (macro_rules based)

Enhancements:
- functions added: cholesky, det, eigh (does not include generalized eigh), eigvalsh (same to eigh), inv, pinv, solve_general, svdvals

author: mrfixit96
body:
## Enhanced Go Development MCP Server

This PR enhances the Go Development MCP Server with the following major improvements:

### Core Architectural Improvements

- **Unified Input Resolution System**: Added an `InputContext` system that provides consistent handling of both code snippets and project paths
- **Strategy Pattern Implementation**: Created separate execution strategies for code snippet execution and project directory execution
- **Enhanced Response Formatting**: Added natural language metadata to help AI assistants better interpret results

### Feature Enhancements

- **Project Path Support**: All tools now accept a `project_path` parameter for working with existing Go project directories
- **Improved Error Handling**: More detailed and helpful error messages with better structure
- **Format Enhancements**: Better go_fmt with support for formatting entire projects

### Documentation

- Updated README with examples of using the new project_path parameter
- Added section on the new features
- Added usage examples for both code snippets and project paths

### Benefits

- **More Flexible Development Workflows**: AI tools can now work with entire Go projects, not just code snippets
- **Cleaner Architecture**: Separation of concerns makes the code more maintainable
- **Better User Experience**: More helpful error messages and structured responses

author: ponyisi
body:
I had misunderstood the concurrency limit in the boto3 configuration as a global limit, but it is only a limit on the number of parallel downloads for each individual download request. Therefore we could still be spawning a huge number of simultaneous S3 connections.

This PR puts semaphores back to limit the number of distinct simultaneous connections. It also tries to reduce the total number of connections made:
* it reuses metadata obtained in the bucket listing,
* it uses a lower level part of the library that means that fewer requests are made.

The new magic numbers are
* maximum 5 simultaneous bucket listings
* maximum 10 distinct files being downloaded simultaneously (configurable)
* maximum 5 download streams per file (internal boto configuration)

author: ishaswm
body:
# fix: Upgrade image processing and tests for detect_lewd_images

## 1. Support multiple Image formats
- Replaced `tf.io.decode_jpeg` with `tf.io.decode_image` which handles JPEG, PNG, WEBP and GIF (static frames only, due to `expand_animations=False`)

## 2. Explicit shape handling
- added `image.set_shape([None, None, 3])` to ensure the tensor has the correct rank (height × width × 3 channels).
- This prevents shape-related errors during preprocessing.
- replaced `tf.get_static_value(preds[0])[0]` with `preds[0].numpy()[0]`,  which is more reliable in modern TensorFlow.

## 3. Better file handling
- Removed forced file deletion and added optional file cleanup.
- Replaced `test_sample_video_from_disk` (was testing images despite the name) with `test_sample_image_from_disk`.

## 4. Improved test robustness
- Expected values were tightly bound (0.10–0.15), Now only asserts that output is a float within the valid probability range (0.0–1.0).
- Explicit float conversion for safety.

## 5. Added new test cases
- `test_invalid_image_path`: Tests error handling
- `test_batch_processing`: Placeholder for future use

author: ranfuan
body:
HP Bar, Enemy Chaser, Damage Mechanism, Engineer Sprite
Added a functional "Slider" HP bar that decreases when player is damaged with it's respective script "HealthSlider" to take care of its functionality. Implemented a script named "EnemyChasePlayer" which can be used on any enemy to chase the player. "EnemyChasePlayer" depends heavily on two "Capsule Colliders (2D)" to function properly. One collider acts like a line of sight which triggers the enemy to give chase to the player. The other collider is to physically check when the enemy comes into contact with another collider (physical object).

The "EnemyDamage" script can be used to customize the amount of damage each "collision" does to the player. This is done by searching for a "HealthSlider" class on the object it collides with. If it collides with the player it will inflict the specified "damage" the "health" variable via the "TakeDamage" function located in the script/class "HealthSlider".

A larva monster was left on the first room entered after the hangar to test all these scripts. It is fully equipped with a "damaging" mechanism and can chase the player via the "EnemyChasePlayer" script. The larva can be duplicated as many times as needed while fully scripted and set up to save time while placing enemies.

Finally, an engineer sprite was added for future use.

author: kmdewaal
body:
According to the PulseAudio Destruction documentation,

"When the PulseAudio connection has been terminated, the thread must be stopped and the resources freed. Stopping the thread is done using
pa_threaded_mainloop_stop(), which must be called
without the lock (see below) held. When that
function returns, the thread is stopped and
the pa_threaded_mainloop object can be freed using pa_threaded_mainloop_free()."

The code in audiooutputpulse.cpp called
pa_threaded_mainloop_stop(), but never called
pa_threaded_mainloop_free(). That missing call is
what frees up allocated resources like FIFO files.

The missing calls to pa_threaded_mainloop_free() have been added in this modification.

Resolves: #1095

1. 修复src/environment/problem/basic_problem.py中numpy数组不具有device属性的问题
修改了 Basic_Problem_Torch.eval 方法，在尝试访问 device 属性之前检查输入类型。如果输入是 NumPy 数组，则转换为 PyTorch 张量并设置默认设备为 CPU。

2. 统一方法命名
将 CEC2013LSGO_Torch_Problem 子类中的 compute 方法重命名为 func，以符合基类定义的抽象方法。这解决了 F5_Torch 到 F15_Torch 类中的继承不一致问题。

3. 修复相对导入路径
修正了 src/baseline/__init__.py 中的相对导入路径，将from metabbo import *改为正确的导入路径from .metabbo import *，解决了模块导入错误。

4. 处理 GLEET 优化器中的 PyTorch 张量
在 gleet_optimizer.py 的 initialize_particles 和 update 方法中添加了类型检查和转换，确保在使用 NumPy 函数前将 PyTorch 张量转换为 NumPy 数组。

以上修改已经过测试，代码正常运行，测试代码如下：
```
from src import Config, Trainer
# import meta-level agent of MetaBBO you want to meta-train
from src.baseline.metabbo import GLEET
# import low-level BBO optimizer of MetaBBO you want to meta-train
from src.environment.optimizer import GLEET_Optimizer
from src.environment.problem.utils import construct_problem_set

# put user-specific configuration
config = {'train_problem': 'lsgo-torch',           'train_batch_size': 1,
          'train_parallel_mode':'dummy', 
          }
config = Config(config)
# construct dataset
config, datasets = construct_problem_set(config)
# initialize your MetaBBO's meta-level agent & low-level optimizer
gleet = GLEET(config)
gleet_opt = GLEET_Optimizer(config)
trainer = Trainer(config, gleet, gleet_opt, datasets)
trainer.train()
```

## Description

Added comprehensive Docker support for the MellowMind application with multi-service architecture. This PR includes:

- Docker configuration for React frontend with Nginx serving optimized static assets
- Docker setup for Node.js backend and Python AI services
- Complete docker-compose.yml for orchestrating all services
- Enhanced networking configuration with dedicated mellow-network
- CORS settings for proper service communication
- Production-ready API configurations in ChatContainer
- Documentation for Docker setup and usage

## Related Issue

Implements - Containerize application services
Resolves  - Docker environment production readiness

## Motivation and Context

Containerization provides consistent environments across development and production, simplifies deployment, and enables easier scaling of services. This implementation forms the foundation for our deployment pipeline and ensures that all team members can run the application in a reliable, consistent environment with proper service communication.

## How Has This Been Tested?

- Full end-to-end testing of the containerized application stack
- Verified container builds and communication between all services
- Tested data persistence and environment variable handling
- Validated frontend-to-backend connectivity through configured Nginx proxy
- Confirmed proper performance in both development and production modes

## Types of Changes

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to change)

## Checklist

- [x] My code follows the code style of this project.
- [x] I have added tests to cover my changes.
- [x] All new and existing tests passed.

### [`v0.34.2`](https://redirect.github.com/huggingface/accelerate/compare/v0.34.1...v0.34.2)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/huggingface/accelerate/compare/v0.34.1...v0.34.2)

### [`v0.34.1`](https://redirect.github.com/huggingface/accelerate/releases/tag/v0.34.1): Patchfix

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/huggingface/accelerate/compare/v0.34.0...v0.34.1)

#### Bug fixes

- Fixes an issue where processed `DataLoaders` could no longer be pickled in [#​3074](https://redirect.github.com/huggingface/accelerate/issues/3074) thanks to [@​byi8220](https://redirect.github.com/byi8220)
- Fixes an issue when using FSDP where `default_transformers_cls_names_to_wrap` would separate `_no_split_modules` by characters instead of keeping it as a list of layer names in [#​3075](https://redirect.github.com/huggingface/accelerate/issues/3075)

**Full Changelog**: <https://github.com/huggingface/accelerate/compare/v0.34.0...v0.34.1>

### [`v0.34.0`](https://redirect.github.com/huggingface/accelerate/releases/tag/v0.34.0): : StatefulDataLoader Support, FP8 Improvements, and PyTorch Updates!

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/huggingface/accelerate/compare/v0.33.0...v0.34.0)

#### Dependency Changes

- **Updated Safetensors Requirement:** The library now requires `safetensors` version 0.4.3.
- **Added support for Numpy 2.0:** The library now fully supports `numpy` 2.0.0

#### Core

##### New Script Behavior Changes

- **Process Group Management:** PyTorch now requires users to destroy process groups after training. The `accelerate` library will handle this automatically with `accelerator.end_training()`, or you can do it manually using `PartialState().destroy_process_group()`.
- **MLU Device Support:** Added support for saving and loading RNG states on MLU devices by [@​huismiling](https://redirect.github.com/huismiling)
- **NPU Support:** Corrected backend and distributed settings when using `transfer_to_npu`, ensuring better performance and compatibility.

##### DataLoader Enhancements

- **Stateful DataDataLoader:** We are excited to announce that early support has been added for the `StatefulDataLoader` from `torchdata`, allowing better handling of data loading states. Enable by passing `use_stateful_dataloader=True` to the `DataLoaderConfiguration`, and when calling `load_state()` the `DataLoader` will automatically be resumed from its last step, no more having to iterate through passed batches.
- **Decoupled Data Loader Preparation:** The `prepare_data_loader()` function is now **independent** of the `Accelerator`, giving you more flexibility towards which API levels you would like to use.
- **XLA Compatibility:** Added support for skipping initial batches when using XLA.
- **Improved State Management:** Bug fixes and enhancements for saving/loading `DataLoader` states, ensuring smoother training sessions.
- **Epoch Setting:** Introduced the `set_epoch` function for `MpDeviceLoaderWrapper`.

##### FP8 Training Improvements

- **Enhanced FP8 Training:** Fully Sharded Data Parallelism (FSDP) and DeepSpeed support now work seamlessly with `TransformerEngine` FP8 training, including better defaults for the quantized FP8 weights.
- **Integration baseline**: We've added a new suite of examples and benchmarks to ensure that our `TransformerEngine` integration works exactly as intended. These scripts run one half using 🤗 Accelerate's integration, the other with raw `TransformersEngine`, providing users with a nice example of what we do under the hood with accelerate, and a good sanity check to make sure nothing breaks down over time. Find them [here](https://redirect.github.com/huggingface/accelerate/tree/main/benchmarks/fp8)
- **Import Fixes:** Resolved issues with import checks for the Transformers Engine that has downstream issues.
- **FP8 Docker Images:** We've added new docker images for `TransformerEngine` and `accelerate` as well. Use `docker pull huggingface/accelerate@gpu-fp8-transformerengine` to quickly get an environment going.

#### `torchpippy` no more, long live `torch.distributed.pipelining`

- With the latest PyTorch release, `torchpippy` is now fully integrated into torch core, and as a result we are **exclusively supporting the PyTorch implementation from now on**
- There are breaking examples and changes that comes from this shift. Namely:
  - Tracing of inputs is done with a shape *each GPU will see*, rather than the size of the total batch. So for 2 GPUs, one should pass in an input of `[1, n, n]` rather than `[2, n, n]` as before.
  - **We no longer support Encoder/Decoder models**. PyTorch tracing for `pipelining` no longer supports encoder/decoder models, so the `t5` example has been removed.
  - **Computer vision model support currently does not work**: There are some tracing issues regarding resnet's we are actively looking into.
- **If either of these changes are too breaking, we recommend pinning your accelerate version**. If the encoder/decoder model support is **actively blocking your inference using pippy**, please open an issue and let us know. We can look towards adding in the old support for `torchpippy` potentially if needed.

#### Fully Sharded Data Parallelism (FSDP)

- **Environment Flexibility:** Environment variables are now **fully optional** for FSDP, simplifying configuration. You can now fully create a `FullyShardedDataParallelPlugin` yourself manually *with no need for environment patching*:

```python
from accelerate import FullyShardedDataParallelPlugin
fsdp_plugin = FullyShardedDataParallelPlugin(...)
```

- **FSDP RAM efficient loading:** Added a utility to enable RAM-efficient model loading (by setting the proper environmental variable). **This is generally needed if not using `accelerate launch` and need to ensure the env variables are setup properly for model loading**:

```python
from accelerate.utils import enable_fsdp_ram_efficient_loading, disable_fsdp_ram_efficient_loading
enable_fsdp_ram_efficient_loading()
```

- **Model State Dict Management:** Enhanced support for unwrapping model state dicts in FSDP, making it easier to manage distributed models.

#### New Examples

- **Configuration and Models:** Improved configuration handling and introduced a configuration zoo for easier experimentation. You can learn more [here](https://redirect.github.com/huggingface/accelerate/tree/main/examples/config_yaml_templates). This was largely inspired by the `axolotl` library, so very big kudos to their wonderful [work](https://redirect.github.com/axolotl-ai-cloud/axolotl/tree/main/examples)
- **FSDP + SLURM Example:** Added a [minimal configuration example for running jobs with SLURM and using FSDP](https://redirect.github.com/huggingface/accelerate/blob/main/examples/slurm/submit_multinode_fsdp.sh)

#### Bug Fixes

- Fix bug of clip\_grad\_norm\_ for xla fsdp by [@​hanwen-sun](https://redirect.github.com/hanwen-sun) in [#​2941](https://redirect.github.com/huggingface/accelerate/pull/2941)
- Explicit check for `step` when loading the state by [@​muellerzr](https://redirect.github.com/muellerzr) in [#​2992](https://redirect.github.com/huggingface/accelerate/pull/2992)
- Fix `find_tied_params` for m

Improved the appointments table allowing users to see the priority of the there appointments

Improved the create appointments code to utilize djiktra algorithm to decide the priority level of appointments, via keyword matching and assigning them automatically to the correct department

Added a referral management system, allowing doctors to create there referrals in case a patient needed one.

I plan to integrate FSM in the referral management in the future.

But for now The system has a working djikstra algorithm already implemented.

Bug to fix in the future when creating appointments, in the view table fix the Date Column. It has correct dates but the time is kinda bugging me.

Improved the looks of the sidebar, to make it more sleek and interactive.

Fixed some bugs in some parts of the system.

Next Update: Swiftly integrate paymongo to the system and create the Invoice Sidebar component later.

This version is highly experimental and maybe buggy so bear in mind.

body:
```python
class Qwen3MoeMLP(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, config, intermediate_size=None):
        super().__init__()
        self.config = config
        self.hidden_size = config.hidden_size
        self.intermediate_size = intermediate_size if intermediate_size is not None else config.intermediate_size
        self.gate_proj = nn.Linear(self.hidden_size, self.intermediate_size, bias=False)
        self.up_proj = nn.Linear(self.hidden_size, self.intermediate_size, bias=False)
        self.down_proj = nn.Linear(self.intermediate_size, self.hidden_size, bias=False)
        self.act_fn = ACT2FN[config.hidden_act]

    def forward(self, x):
        down_proj = self.down_proj(self.act_fn(self.gate_proj(x)) * self.up_proj(x))
        return down_proj
```

In Qwen3 MoE, the MLP module is created with two possible intermediate sizes. The sparse MoE block uses MLP with size `config.moe_intermediate_size` while the decoder layer uses MLP with size `config.intermediate_size`.

This is also observed in DeepseekV3 and likely many more MoE models to come. Therefore we extend this flexibility to LitGPT's own MLP modules.

author: bakura10
body:
Fixes #3207

Last year, Shopify introduced a massive bug to the cart endpoints, that took several weeks and a lot of effort on my end to have the issue properly investigated and fixed by Shopify. This bug was reproducible on all documented Ajax endpoints (https://shopify.dev/docs/api/ajax/reference/cart#get-locale-cart-js).

Since last week, another important regression has been introduced to the documented Cart Ajax API, where products can't be removed and their quantity can't be changed from the cart (!!) as soon as you are in a market URL containing a country and language (such as mysite.com/en-fr).

The problem is that, for some reason, Dawn (and all other themes built on top of Dawn) are using undocumented endpoints to interact with the Cart. It looked to me initially that the `cart/xxx` and `cart/xxx.js` endpoints are more or less alias, but there are definitely not. It is the second time in one year where a critical regression is introduced that only happens on the `/cart/xxx.js` documented endpoints, but not on the `/cart/xxx` undocumented endpoints.

Please note that, as per the official Ajax documentation (https://shopify.dev/docs/api/ajax/reference/cart), all Ajax API calls must be made with the .js suffix. There are no mention on being able to use the non-JS URL in Ajax. The non `.js` routes are supposed to be used only when POSTing in the browser.

## Why this change

The main problem is that, when such issues arise, merchants are contacting Shopify support. Shopify support proceeds to a very basic debugging by trying to reproduce the merchant's issue in Dawn, found that it works on Dawn but not on our themes, and concludes the issue is coming from our theme (when it is not). It is nearly impossible for merchants to escalate the issue to a technical team at Shopify, so we end up having to explain to merchant, and try to find someone working at Shopify to investigate the issue. This takes time, cause a lot of frustration on both merchant and our side, and can cost merchants a lot of money as this is about critical parts of the system (the cart).

I am sure that, when releasing a new feature, the Shopify dev team also just test the feature on Dawn, as this is by far the most installed theme in the platform.

Ensuring that Dawn is using documented endpoints (the same as most themes following the docs) will ensure that such bugs can be spotted sooner, and that such issues can be reproduced by the support team at Shopify when testing in Dawn.

## Why not updating our themes to use undocumented endpoints?

One might argue that it would be easier for us to update our code. The problem is that I've been always extremely reluctant to use undocumented endpoints for anything critical. Dawn might be using it, which gives some guarantee that it won't break, but still, it is not documented, and as a consequence we have no guarantee on the exact behavior of those endpoints, nothing to back us up when reaching the technical team.

body:
Summary:
- while loading state dict, convert id from local to global, so when table is resharded, no need to shift id based on sharding decision
- enable load state dict mode for checkpoint loading. 
Since checkpoint client does not support ordered tensor loading, we implemented a short term solution to cache all id, weight and bucket tensor in memory, and after all data are loaded, apply everything to backend.

The current solution is to cache all data in python tensor, here is the flow to use these interfaces:
  - set self.local_weight_counts based on checkpoint bucket tensor size
  - enable_load_state_dict_mode to initialize local cache tensor
  - call state_dict to get empty tensors from checkpoint loader
  - write checkpoint data to cached tensors by checkpoint loader
  - call apply_state_dict to write all cached tensor to backend
    - in apply_state_dict:
      - if optimizer offloading is enabled:
        - for loop chunk of weight and optimizer
        - concat weight and optimizer together
        - write to backend through KVTensorWrapper interface
      - if optimizer offloading is disabled:
        - set optimizer to device tensor based on id
        - write id weight to backend

With this solution is that, when write data to backend, the python tensor's memory cannot be released until all tensor data is duplicated in backend. In a short time, there will have one table's weight tensor be duplicated, we need to make sure the memory capacity is enough.
In addition, with optimizer offloading, we need to concat weight and optimizer together before we can write to backend, since the input data need to be contiguous. To avoid triple the memory consumption, we write chunk data in a for loop, which will cause write performance regression.

After the first version e2e is ready, we'll support unordered loading from backend to improve performance and also reduce memory overhead.

**Saving State Dict**
When saving state dict, we convert IDs from local to global. This allows us to avoid shifting IDs based on sharding decisions when tables are resharded.

**Checkpoint Loading Mode**
We have enabled load state dict mode for checkpoint loading, which allows us to cache all ID, weight, and bucket tensors in memory before applying them to the backend. This approach ensures that all data is loaded correctly, even though the checkpoint client does not support ordered tensor loading.

**Current Solution**
The current solution involves caching all data in Python tensors, following these steps:
- Set self.local_weight_counts based on checkpoint bucket tensor size.
- Enable load state dict mode to initialize local cache tensors.
- Call state_dict to get empty tensors for the checkpoint loader.
- Write checkpoint data to cached tensors from persisted checkpoint by the checkpoint loader.
- Call apply_state_dict to write all cached tensors to the backend.

**Apply State Dict Flow**
During the apply_state_dict step, we perform the following operations:
- If optimizer offloading is enabled:
  - Loop through chunks of weight and optimizer.
  - Concatenate weight and optimizer together.
  - Write to backend using KVTensorWrapper interface.
- If optimizer offloading is disabled:
  - Set optimizer to device tensor based on ID.
  - Write ID weight to backend for each table.

**Limitations**
The current solution has two limitations:
- Memory overhead: 
  - When writing data to the backend, the Python tensor's memory cannot be released until the whole tensor data is duplicated in the backend. This can lead to high memory usage, especially when dealing with single large tables.
- Performance regression: 
  - With optimizer offloading, we need to concatenate weight and optimizer together before writing to the backend. To avoid triple one large tensor's memory, we loop through smaller chunks during writing, which can cause performance regression.

**Future Improvements**
After the first version e2e is ready, we plan to support unordered loading from the backend to improve performance and reduce memory overhead.

# Fix: Use documents_vss table with vss_search for vector similarity search

## Problem
The search functionality was always returning the beginning of text files instead of relevant content when searching for terms like "2025年". This was happening because the search implementation was not properly utilizing the SQLite VSS (Vector Similarity Search) extension.

## Solution
Modified the `search` method in `rag_system.ts` to:
1. Use the `documents_vss` virtual table instead of the `documents` table
2. Implement the `vss_search` function in the WHERE clause as recommended in the SQLite VSS documentation
3. Properly order results by distance for accurate similarity search

## Changes
- Changed SQL query to use `documents_vss` table with `vss_search` function
- Simplified column selection in the query

## Testing
Unable to test locally due to Deno not being installed on the system, but the implementation follows the recommended pattern from the SQLite VSS documentation.

# Implementación de Pipeline CI/CD para Backend

## Descripción
Esta PR implementa un pipeline de CI/CD completo en GitHub Actions que se activa cuando se realiza un push a una rama con un Pull Request abierto, permitiendo automatizar pruebas, build y despliegue del backend en una instancia EC2.

## Características implementadas
- **Verificación de PR abierto**: El pipeline solo se ejecuta cuando existe un PR abierto para la rama actual
- **Pruebas automatizadas**: Ejecución de tests unitarios para garantizar la calidad del código
- **Generación de build**: Compilación del código TypeScript a JavaScript
- **Despliegue continuo**: Transferencia del build a instancia EC2 y reinicio del servicio

## Configuración necesaria
Para el correcto funcionamiento del pipeline, se requieren los siguientes secrets en el repositorio:
- EC2_SSH_PRIVATE_KEY
- EC2_HOST
- EC2_USER

## Requisitos en EC2
- Node.js y npm instalados
- PM2 instalado globalmente para gestión de procesos

This requires a SFTP service. A raspberry pi on the local network is sufficent for testing, but [Azure Blob Storage can also provides a testing scenario](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/blobs/secure-file-transfer-protocol-support).

#### DLL install process
1. Download these two nuget packages:

2. Extract the DLL's:
`lib\net8.0\Renci.SshNet.dll`
`lib\net6.0\BouncyCastle.Cryptography.dll`
3. Place in service tier's `Add-Ins`-folder and in one of the `al.assemblyProbingPaths`.

My internal checklist for this PR:
- [x] Get approval of SSH.NET + BouncyCastle.Cryptography for Business Central

This pull request focuses on optimizing image loading for the hero block in a WordPress theme and includes a version update. The changes aim to improve performance by conditionally loading images and hiding unnecessary elements to reduce resource usage.

### Optimizations for image loading:

author: janetgoodswill
body:
## Overview
This PR implements a tokenized workforce development platform using Clarity smart contracts. The platform consists of five main contracts that work together to create a comprehensive system for worker verification, skill assessment, training recommendations, progress tracking, and certification.

## Contracts Implemented

### 1. Individual Verification Contract
- Validates and stores worker identities
- Provides verification status with expiry dates
- Allows admin to verify and revoke verification

### 2. Skill Assessment Contract
- Records verified capabilities of workers
- Manages a catalog of skills with descriptions and categories
- Allows assessment of worker proficiency with evidence

### 3. Training Recommendation Contract
- Matches workers with education opportunities
- Manages a catalog of training programs
- Provides personalized recommendations based on skill gaps

### 4. Progress Tracking Contract
- Records skill development progress
- Tracks enrollment in training programs
- Records milestones with verification

### 5. Certification Contract
- Validates completed training
- Issues certificates with optional expiry dates
- Provides verification mechanism for certificates

## Testing
- Comprehensive test suite using Vitest
- Tests cover all main contract functions
- Mocks the Clarity environment for testing

## Security Considerations
- Admin controls for sensitive operations
- Verification expiry to ensure up-to-date information
- Proper access controls for data modification

## Next Steps
- Integration with frontend UI
- Implementation of token economics
- Enhanced privacy features
- Integration with external training providers

author: nwoguglory1
body:
Pull Request Description:
This update introduces a comprehensive set of features designed to streamline and enhance the decentralized marketplace for freelancer projects. The following enhancements have been implemented:

Milestone Management:

Introduced milestone tracking to allow structured task management for jobs.
Integrated status updates, payment transfers, and progress tracking for seamless management of ongoing tasks.
Enhanced the job completion process with feedback mechanisms such as ratings and comments.
Advanced Search and Categorization:

Developed a job tagging system to enable efficient filtering and discovery.
Implemented the ability to categorize jobs and retrieve jobs by category for better organization.
Freelancer Tools:

Added features to manage freelancer availability, including schedules and weekly working hours.
Integrated a bookmarking system for users to save and revisit job opportunities.
Enabled freelancers to log their working hours and view detailed time logs.
User Profile and Skill Management:

Introduced functionality for freelancers to update their skill sets and manage their profiles effectively.
Enhanced user experience with utilities for creating, updating, and retrieving profile details.
Data-Driven Insights:

Developed helper functions to retrieve job-related data, including bids, ratings, milestones, and freelancer skills.
These enhancements aim to deliver a more structured, transparent, and user-friendly experience for clients and freelancers.

The compiler state doesn't accurately represent the actual state, as the parameters are set by the compiler only when the user compiles. This fix allows the code parser to respond correctly to the changes in configuration and also adds the custom config file. It also responds to changes in that file. 

Can be tested by cloning remix-reward. the main file should show yellow lines when optimization is off. Now it will react properly to changes in the UI and also to changing custom config files.

body:
## 概要
プロジェクト全体で使用しているパッケージマネージャーをbunからnpmに移行しました。

## 変更内容
- CIワークフローでbunの代わりにNode.js/npmを使用するよう変更
- 各ディレクトリのbun.lockを削除し、package-lock.jsonを生成
- frontend/package.jsonの`bun run`を`npm run`に変更
- ドキュメント（README.md、CLAUDE.md）のコマンド例を更新
- Dependabot設定をbunからnpmに変更

## 修正内容
- `setup-node`のバージョン指定を修正（SHA指定から`v4`に変更）
- CIで`npm install`の代わりに`npm ci`を使用するよう修正
- package-lock.jsonを再生成してプラットフォーム固有のバイナリ問題を解決

## 理由
- より広い環境での互換性と安定性を確保
- 一般的なJavaScript/Node.jsエコシステムとの統合を改善

## テスト
- [x] APIのユニットテストがパス
- [x] 各ディレクトリでlintが正常に実行
- [x] 依存関係のインストールが成功
- [x] CIが正常に動作

## Summary

Use an HTML comment for notational pieces of the PR template

## Details

- very similar to an old PR of mine in a different repo: https://github.com/argoproj/argo-helm/pull/1969
- the notes about versioned docs are purely notational, i.e. have nothing to fill out
  - comment them out with HTML comments, as is common practice
    - example from a repo I maintain: https://github.com/ezolenko/rollup-plugin-typescript2/blob/f6db59613a66f58c48310aa8fa785951970b5d6d/.github/issue_template.md?plain=1#L2
      - I copied that from other repos too
  - these comments are still visible to the PR author, just not visible when rendered, keeping the PR more concise

Can see an example of what this looks like below vvv. If a maintainer clicks the edit button, will be able to see that the note is still there, just commented out and invisible when rendered.

<!-- 

# READ ME PLEASE

> **TL;DR: Make sure to add your changes to versioned docs**

Thanks for opening a PR!

The docs cover several versions of `react-navigation`, and in some cases there are several files (for version 1, version 2 and etc.) that all describe a single page of the docs (eg. "Getting Started").

Please make sure that the edit you're making in `docs/file-you-edited.md` is also included in the file for the correct version, eg. `/versioned_docs/version-3.x/file-you-edited.md` for version 3. If such file doesn't exist, please create it. :+1:

author: therobbrennan
body:
## Description

This PR introduces a new workflow that fetches NASA's Astronomy Picture of the Day (APOD) and sends it as an MMS message via Twilio. The workflow is designed to run daily and handles both image and video content types from NASA's APOD API.

### Key Features
- **Daily APOD Delivery**: Automatically fetches and sends the latest NASA APOD
- **Multi-format Support**: Handles both image and video content types
- **Rich Media MMS**: Sends high-quality media with formatted captions
- **Informative Content**: Includes title, explanation, and copyright information
- **Scheduled Execution**: Runs once per day to deliver fresh content

## Type of Change

version: feat     # New feature (minor version bump)

## Testing

- [x] I have tested these changes locally using `act`
- [x] All existing tests pass
- [x] My commits are signed with GPG

## Screenshots & Demo

![screencast](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5960e4cf-e252-4f68-8189-05b8714c7d5f)


## Setup Instructions

1. **NASA API Key**
   - Get a free API key from [NASA API Portal](https://api.nasa.gov/)
   - Add it to your `.env` file as `NASA_API_KEY`

2. **Twilio Configuration**
   - Set up Twilio credentials in your `.env` file:
     ```
     # Twilio Configuration
     TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID=your_twilio_account_sid_here
     TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SECRET=your_twilio_account_secret_here
     ```

## Notes
- The workflow includes comprehensive error handling for API failures
- Environment variables are used for all sensitive configuration
- The README includes detailed setup instructions and examples

# Add `z.looseEnum()` for permissive enum validation

## Fixes #4362  - Request for permissive enum validation

Introduces a new `z.looseEnum()` validator that provides more flexible input validation while maintaining type safety.

### Key Features
- ✅ Preserves TypeScript type hints for preferred values
- ✅ Accepts any string input (unlike strict `z.enum()`)
- 🔗 Seamless integration with other Zod validators
- 🏗 Designed for permissive request validation

## Usage

```typescript
// Basic usage
const StatusSchema = z.looseEnum(['pending', 'completed']);
StatusSchema.parse('pending');  // valid
StatusSchema.parse('other');    // also valid
StatusSchema.parse(123);        // throws ZodError

// With object schemas
const RequestSchema = z.object({
  status: z.looseEnum(['on', 'off']),
  id: z.string()
});

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

author: julik
body:
and ensure it does not contain dots. "Instance name" is the terminology used by some mDNS browsers, it is basically the service name sans the service component.

The service name may include all sorts of characters except for the separator (the dot), and it may include spaces. If one wants to expose a service on a .local subdomain (for example - for Rails testing) - deriving the service name from the hostname _may_ work, but it is easier to make it settable explicitly. Devices like printers do that as well. If you try to advertize a service with dots in it, it will be considered a "different type of service" and in my experience such records just don't end up getting honored.

Another option would be to replace all dots in the service name before the service type with, say, dashes - that would be more automatic, but it is neat that the service name can be "art-directed".

Remove the .local component from the passed hostname, because it seems redundant - we only advertise the fully-qualified hostname, to which we append .local. anyway.

Description:
---
The action to update Taxes and Accounts when changing the fiscal pos on invoice isn't considering the change in price_unit for lines with price included taxes.

Steps to Reproduce:
---
1- Create a 21% tax and another 6% tax, both are included in price
2- Create a fiscal position that will map the 21% tax by the 6% tax
3- Create a product with Price = 121€, and Tax = 21%
4- Create an invoice with this product.
5- On the (Other info) tab, set the Fiscal Position to the one created (from 21 to 6).
6- Click on update taxes and accounts: 
The price will still be 121 while the taxes will change to 6%, and total = 121.
7- Then if you added a new line with the product now after setting the fiscal pos , you will get
price= 106, tax=6%, total = 106. which are the right values.

Cause:
---
The action created for updating taxes and accounts didn't consider price changes for price included taxes.

Fix:
---
Add call to _compute_price_unit()

This pull request introduces significant changes to integrate Azure Service Bus into the `Home.AvaliacaoTecnica` application. It adds configuration, abstraction layers, and updates to existing services and tests to support the new messaging functionality. The most important changes are grouped into the following themes:

### Azure Service Bus Integration

* Added `ServiceBusConfigurationBuilder` to configure Service Bus senders and processors with dependency injection (`Home.AvaliacaoTecnica.Application/Config/ServiceBusConfigurationBuilder.cs`).
* Introduced `ServiceBusConstants` to centralize Service Bus connection string and client name constants (`Home.AvaliacaoTecnica.Application/Config/ServiceBusConstants.cs`).
* Added `ServiceCollectionExtensions` to simplify the registration of Azure Service Bus configurations (`Home.AvaliacaoTecnica.Application/Config/ServiceCollectionExtensions.cs`).

### Updates to Command Handling

* Refactored `EnviarPedidoCommandHandler` to use the new `IServiceBusSenderWrapper` abstraction for sending messages, replacing the previous `IServiceBusSenderFactory` (`Home.AvaliacaoTecnica.Application/Pedido/EnviarPedido/EnviarPedidoCommandHandler.cs`). [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-2dc262f9d90ba244c3a4fb66b71e4ae2802ac26ac20f525e6ccc13dc587aeeebL3-R3) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-2dc262f9d90ba244c3a4fb66b71e4ae2802ac26ac20f525e6ccc13dc587aeeebL15-L36) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-2dc262f9d90ba244c3a4fb66b71e4ae2802ac26ac20f525e6ccc13dc587aeeebL50-R51)

### Abstraction Layers for Messaging

* Added `IServiceBusSenderWrapper` interface and its implementation `ServiceBusSenderWrapper` to encapsulate Service Bus sender configuration and message sending (`Home.AvaliacaoTecnica.Application/Services/Wrapper/IServiceBusSenderWrapper.cs`, `Home.AvaliacaoTecnica.Application/Services/Wrapper/ServiceBusSenderWrapper.cs`). [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-e29614b9afa08de8039ae11966e4ee0df2ea90281a1a28536999fa249201528fR1-R19) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-a2cab01ab86940d4dead70be062472e972dfff619a26b261bf14654de02da57aR1-R28)

### Unit Test Updates

* Updated `EnviarPedidoCommandHandlerTests` to mock and test the new `IServiceBusSenderWrapper` instead of the previous `IServiceBusSenderFactory` (`Home.AvaliacaoTecnica.Domain.Unit/EnviarPedido/EnviarPedidoCommandHandlerTests.cs`). [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-ace99daee3d9d1967acb79e76be38c02918d35518bcc2add193bd0c02271bfb7L18-R33) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-ace99daee3d9d1967acb79e76be38c02918d35518bcc2add193bd0c02271bfb7L60-R61) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-ace99daee3d9d1967acb79e76be38c02918d35518bcc2add193bd0c02271bfb7R108-L108)

### Miscellaneous Improvements

* Added a method `GetImpostoStrategyName` to `PedidoService` and updated the `ImpostoStrategyFactory` to use direct dependencies instead of `IServiceProvider` (`Home.AvaliacaoTecnica.Domain/Services/PedidoService.cs`, `Home.AvaliacaoTecnica.Domain/Strategies/ImpostoStrategyFactory.cs`). [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-bdd37e9b053394c958053ce665b280a0e5bf4f52c8f7b63c4ef2362dac393194R20-R24) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-456b26f0a916cef7e095c5d4639114abea417e4e8ee336bba0245d18500da885L2-R17)
* Updated the solution file to include the new `Testing.AzureServiceBus` project (`Home,AvaliacaoTecnica.sln`). ([Home,AvaliacaoTecnica.slnR30-R31](diffhunk://#diff-1f325fe7e42976a238be27adb7294572de9457ba25355d9bb259e1a112b0a439R30-R31), [Home,AvaliacaoTecnica.slnR74-R77](diffhunk://#diff-1f325fe7e42976a238be27adb7294572de9457ba25355d9bb259e1a112b0a439R74-R77), [Home,AvaliacaoTecnica.slnR87](diffhunk://#diff-1f325fe7e42976a238be27adb7294572de9457ba25355d9bb259e1a112b0a439R87))

body:
This pull request introduces Azure Service Bus integration into the application, refactors existing messaging logic, and enhances the tax calculation service. The most significant changes include adding a Service Bus configuration builder and wrapper, replacing the `IServiceBusSenderFactory` with a new abstraction, and updating the tax service to include strategy name retrieval.

### Azure Service Bus Integration:

* Added `ServiceBusConfigurationBuilder` to simplify configuration of Service Bus clients, senders, and processors (`Home.AvaliacaoTecnica.Application/Config/ServiceBusConfigurationBuilder.cs`).
* Introduced `ServiceBusConstants` for centralized management of Service Bus connection strings and client names (`Home.AvaliacaoTecnica.Application/Config/ServiceBusConstants.cs`).
* Added `ServiceCollectionExtensions` to register Azure Service Bus clients and configurations (`Home.AvaliacaoTecnica.Application/Config/ServiceCollectionExtensions.cs`).
* Updated `Home.AvaliacaoTecnica.Application.csproj` to include the `Microsoft.Extensions.Azure` package for Azure Service Bus support.

### Refactoring Messaging Logic:

* Replaced `IServiceBusSenderFactory` with `IServiceBusSenderWrapper`, which provides better encapsulation and simplifies message sending (`Home.AvaliacaoTecnica.Application/Services/Wrapper/IServiceBusSenderWrapper.cs`, `Home.AvaliacaoTecnica.Application/Services/Wrapper/ServiceBusSenderWrapper.cs`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-e29614b9afa08de8039ae11966e4ee0df2ea90281a1a28536999fa249201528fR1-R19) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-a2cab01ab86940d4dead70be062472e972dfff619a26b261bf14654de02da57aR1-R28).
* Refactored `EnviarPedidoCommandHandler` to use `IServiceBusSenderWrapper` for sending messages (`Home.AvaliacaoTecnica.Application/Pedido/EnviarPedido/EnviarPedidoCommandHandler.cs`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-2dc262f9d90ba244c3a4fb66b71e4ae2802ac26ac20f525e6ccc13dc587aeeebL3-R3) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-2dc262f9d90ba244c3a4fb66b71e4ae2802ac26ac20f525e6ccc13dc587aeeebL15-L36) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-2dc262f9d90ba244c3a4fb66b71e4ae2802ac26ac20f525e6ccc13dc587aeeebL50-R51).

### Enhancements to Tax Service:

* Added a method to `IPedidoService` and `PedidoService` to retrieve the name of the current tax strategy (`Home.AvaliacaoTecnica.Domain/Services/IPedidoService.cs`, `Home.AvaliacaoTecnica.Domain/Services/PedidoService.cs`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-2562ba8dba274eee27301fe73878846a1f23dbea93ecbf54dd70e92c704297afR6-R7) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-bdd37e9b053394c958053ce665b280a0e5bf4f52c8f7b63c4ef2362dac393194R20-R24).
* Simplified `ImpostoStrategyFactory` by removing dependency on `IServiceProvider` and directly injecting strategies (`Home.AvaliacaoTecnica.Domain/Strategies/ImpostoStrategyFactory.cs`).

These changes collectively improve the application's messaging capabilities, simplify configuration and testing, and enhance the flexibility of the tax calculation service.

author: toor1245
body:
Github actions added support Windows Arm64 for public repositories with runner name `windows-11-arm`:

- [Windows arm64 hosted runners now available in public preview](https://github.blog/changelog/2025-04-14-windows-arm64-hosted-runners-now-available-in-public-preview/)
- [Windows 11 by Arm Limited installed packages](https://github.com/actions/partner-runner-images/blob/main/images/arm-windows-11-image.md)

Cmake has known issue related to build for Windows Arm64. `CMAKE_SYSTEM_PROCESSOR` on Arm64 target shows `AMD64`...

- https://github.com/toor1245/cpu_features/actions/runs/15084083163/job/42404469826#step:3:14

Issue discussion:
- https://gitlab.kitware.com/cmake/cmake/-/issues/15170
- https://gitlab.kitware.com/cmake/cmake/-/issues/25466

So `CMAKE_<LANG>_COMPILER_ARCHITECTURE_ID` must be used to set  `PROCESSOR_IS_AARCH64` architecture:
- https://cmake.org/cmake/help/latest/variable/CMAKE_SYSTEM_PROCESSOR.html
- https://cmake.org/cmake/help/v3.16/variable/CMAKE_LANG_COMPILER_ARCHITECTURE_ID.html

Also, currently we have build fail for windows Arm64, I think it should be fixed as separate patch:
- One of the solution is to add check - https://github.com/google/cpu_features/pull/353
- Another way is just copy `LINE` features from [src/impl_aarch64__base_implementation.inl#L31](https://github.com/google/cpu_features/blob/main/src/impl_aarch64__base_implementation.inl#L31)
- just to remind the root cause maybe we will find universal solution, https://github.com/google/cpu_features/pull/291 :


We can't use "define_introspection_and_hwcaps.inl" as a common file for all operating systems due to msvc compiler error C2099: initializer is not a constant, so as a workaround for Windows I used separate "define_introspection.inl"

Code largely borrowed from https://github.com/Bubberstation/Bubberstation/pull/2988 niko getting that bag

import turtle
import time
import math
from datetime import datetime

class Watch:
    def __init__(self):
        self.running = True

    def update(self):
        pass

class Цифра:
    def __init__(self, x, y, текст):
        self.x = x
        self.y = y
        self.текст = текст
        self.малюй()

    def малюй(self):
        t = turtle.Turtle()
        t.hideturtle()
        t.penup()
        t.goto(self.x, self.y)
        t.write(self.текст, align="center", font=("Arial", 14, "normal"))

class Циферблат:
    def __init__(self, радіус=200):
        self.радіус = радіус
        self.малюй_циферблат()

    def малюй_циферблат(self):
        turtle.mode("logo")
        for i in range(1, 13):
            кут = math.radians(i * 30)
            x = self.радіус * math.sin(кут)
            y = self.радіус * math.cos(кут)
            Цифра(x, y, str(i))

class Стрілка:
    def __init__(self, довжина, товщина, колір):
        self.довжина = довжина
        self.курсор = turtle.Turtle()
        self.курсор.hideturtle()
        self.курсор.speed(0)
        self.курсор.pensize(товщина)
        self.курсор.color(колір)

    def малюй(self, кут):
        self.курсор.clear()
        self.курсор.penup()
        self.курсор.goto(0, 0)
        self.курсор.setheading(90)
        self.курсор.right(кут)
        self.курсор.pendown()
        self.курсор.forward(self.довжина)

class AnalogWatch(Watch):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        Циферблат()
        self.годин = Стрілка(100, 6, "black")
        self.хвилин = Стрілка(140, 3, "blue")
        self.секунд = Стрілка(160, 1, "red")
        self.update()

    def update(self):
        now = datetime.now()
        s = now.second
        m = now.minute
        h = now.hour % 12 + m / 60
        self.секунд.малюй(s * 6)
        self.хвилин.малюй(m * 6)
        self.годин.малюй(h * 30)
        turtle.ontimer(self.update, 1000)

class DigitalWatch(Watch):
    def __init__(self, формат_24=True):
        super().__init__()
        self.формат_24 = формат_24
        self.text = turtle.Turtle()
        self.text.hideturtle()
        self.text.penup()
        self.text.goto(0, -250)
        self.text.color("green")
        self.update()

    def update(self):
        now = datetime.now()
        h = now.hour
        m = now.minute
        s = now.second
        if not self.формат_24:
            suffix = "AM" if h < 12 else "PM"
            h = h % 12 or 12
            time_str = f"{h:02}:{m:02}:{s:02} {suffix}"
        else:
            time_str = f"{h:02}:{m:02}:{s:02}"
        self.text.clear()
        self.text.write(time_str, align="center", font=("Courier", 20, "bold"))
        turtle.ontimer(self.update, 1000)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    turtle.Screen().bgcolor("white")
    AnalogWatch()
    DigitalWatch(формат_24=False)
    turtle.mainloop()

author: aldi-h
body:
This pull request introduces updates to the project's code formatting and linting configurations to improve code readability and enforce stricter naming conventions. The main changes include enhancements to the Prettier configuration for handling Tailwind CSS and updates to the ESLint configuration to prevent abbreviations in variable names.

### Prettier Configuration Updates:
* Added new Tailwind CSS-specific options to `.prettierrc`, including `tailwindStylesheet`, `tailwindAttributes`, `tailwindFunctions`, and `tailwindPreserveDuplicates`, to better handle Tailwind CSS styling and utilities.
* Reordered the `plugins` array in `.prettierrc` to ensure compatibility between `prettier-plugin-tailwindcss` and `@trivago/prettier-plugin-sort-imports`.

### ESLint Configuration Updates:
* Enabled the `unicorn/prevent-abbreviations` rule in `eslint.config.mjs` to enforce the use of full, descriptive names instead of abbreviations. Custom replacements were defined for common abbreviations like `err` (to `error`), `msg` (to `message`), and `res` (to `response`, `resource`, or `result`)

author: c0d3-m4513r
body:
The Graph-Renderer is of order O(n) (approximately it takes 1 ms per ~1.000 data_points). Some efforts should be taken to improve the performance in that region, especially when you can easily reach 1.000.000 data points (which take 1s to process).

To optimize the Graph-Renderer two approaches were taken:
1. The min and max values for the x and y axis are calculated by only searching for new min/max values on the new data-points
2. The generation of paths using d3 was moved into a web-worker, to free up the main thread for other work (like accepting data over the websocket, processing user input and relayouting/repainting)

Because of https://github.com/AI-Gruppe/OmnAIScope-DataServer/issues/32 I decided to use https://github.com/C0D3-M4513R/OmniDevice for interfacing with the scope.

author: samuelleutner
body: ## Problem Description This PR addresses a notification rendering issue observed in environments like dots-hyprland using ags, where certain notifications, particularly those originating from browsers like Brave or applications like WhatsApp Web, were being displayed with raw HTML content. This included visible tags such as ``, leading to a garbled and unintended display that hinders readability. `[Notification displaying: web.whatsapp.com message]` ![closed_notification](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bf8d96a4-43ff-4480-b0c0-c0ecb4c4b5b8) ![notification](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6c876532-aa5a-4942-bbba-b6123ebacf94) ## Proposed Solution To resolve this issue robustly and centrally, the logic within the `processNotificationBody` function has been enhanced. This function, responsible for preparing the notification content before display, now includes a step to actively filter and remove potential HTML tags from the notification body. A regular expression `/<[^>]*>/g` is applied within `processNotificationBody` to strip all HTML tags. This ensures that, regardless of the notification's origin (even if it contains unexpected markup), only the pure and clean text will be passed to the display widgets. This approach is favored as it consolidates the sanitization logic in a single, dedicated function, making the notification handling more predictable and maintainable. ## How to Test 1. Trigger notifications from applications known to sometimes include HTML in their body, such as receiving a message on WhatsApp Web or getting a notification from a website in Brave browser. 2. Verify that the notification popups or list entries display the message content correctly, without any visible HTML tags, showing only the intended text. ## Additional Considerations * Implementing the HTML filtering within the `processNotificationBody` function provides a centralized and cleaner way to handle potential markup compared to adjusting properties on multiple display widgets. * This sanitization step enhances the overall robustness and security of the notification system by preventing the rendering of arbitrary HTML that might be included in notification payloads, intentionally or not. * While the issue was particularly noticeable with Brave and WhatsApp Web, this solution provides a general safeguard against unexpected HTML in notifications from any source.

body:
**Add configurable gradient support for progress bar**

This PR introduces a new `--gradient (-g)` flag that allows users to customize the progress bar gradient. Users can now select from predefined presets (default, sunset, aqua, forest, fire) or specify two custom hex colors separated by a comma (e.g., --gradient=#00FF00,#0000FF). If the flag is not set or an invalid value is provided, the default gradient is used.

**Features:**

New --gradient flag for selecting gradient style.
Support for both presets and custom color pairs.
Updated help text to document the new flag.

author: arthurmoreno
body:
This pull request introduces several updates across the codebase, including enhancements to the build system, new functionality for genome and attribute handling, and minor code style improvements. The most notable changes focus on adding new classes and methods for genome configuration and attributes, improving maintainability and extensibility. Additionally, linting configuration and Python-specific build commands were added.

### Build System Enhancements:
* Added new `Makefile` targets: `clean`, `py-build`, and `clean-py-build` to streamline Python package building and cleanup processes. (`Makefile`, [MakefileR10-R29](diffhunk://#diff-76ed074a9305c04054cdebb9e9aad2d818052b07091de1f20cad0bbac34ffb52R10-R29))

### Genome and Attribute Handling:
* Introduced new classes in `src/genome.hpp` and `src/genome.cpp` for genome configuration (`DefaultGenomeConfig`) and genome representation (`DefaultGenome`), along with methods for mutation, connection setup, and node creation. (`src/genome.hpp`, [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-8469abde49a2892bbff76aab005ad6b08883cecd7d90aaaaf692c0143d51366bR1-R93); `src/genome.cpp`, [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-6f3f20e19bff24a18261a3a2ade5a06700fa817227b8619aafdfa8be4f735343R1-R144)
* Added a comprehensive `BaseAttribute` class and its derived classes (`FloatAttribute`, `IntegerAttribute`, `BoolAttribute`, `StringAttribute`) in `src/attributes.hpp`, providing functionality for initialization, mutation, and validation of various attribute types. (`src/attributes.hpp`, [src/attributes.hppR1-R302](diffhunk://#diff-6a32d421596ee41965c4363d093cca341e6340a735938e6d8aa7031dc3ad81d0R1-R302))

### Linting and Code Style:
* Added `ruff` configuration in `pyproject.toml` for linting, specifying rules for line length, target Python version, and exclusions. (`pyproject.toml`, [pyproject.tomlR52-R61](diffhunk://#diff-50c86b7ed8ac2cf95bd48334961bf0530cdc77b5a56f852c5c61b89d735fd711R52-R61))
* Refactored long parameter lists and dictionary definitions across multiple files for better readability. (`src/neat3p/aggregations.py`, [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-2b66769e31b129c7907654c50f5cc1cda71b9555e9f5923f8ad51df02a2cc699L79-R82); `src/neat3p/attributes.py`, [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-f220966cbacce21f4d7dd8a005f994fb7a793bd20fec1d4e8ff57a1d48ba474fL179-R190) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-f220966cbacce21f4d7dd8a005f994fb7a793bd20fec1d4e8ff57a1d48ba474fL189-R204); `src/neat3p/checkpoint.py`, [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-5f2e30ab82a00700f1bed32e1829fae52f7b70e3c43905debef6a0e3fb769889L18-R23)

### Minor Fixes:

author: ikappaki
body:
Hi,

can you please consider patch to mare assertion rewrite warning messages filterable using the standard `-W` option. It addresses #5473.

The issue arises when a Python package defines a `pytest` plugin, and also calls `pytest.main()` programmatically, after importing one of its own submodules. Because the module is already imported, `pytest.main()` cannot rewrite its assertions and emits a warning like:

```Module already imported so cannot be rewritten: basilisp```

Unfortunately, the `:` in the message conflicts with Python’s warning filter syntax, where `:` is used as a delimiter. This prevents users from filtering out the warning via `-W`.

This patch replaces the `:` in the warning message with a `;`, making it possible to write a valid warning filter like:

`-W ignore:Module already imported so cannot be rewritten; mymodule:pytest.PytestAssertRewriteWarning`

We believe there's no need to force assertion rewriting simply because a module defines a plugin, and users should be able to suppress this warning when needed.

For background and alternative solutions considered, see https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/5473#issuecomment-2874319476.

author: pookjw
body:
This PR ensures thread safety when a `URLSession.data(for:)` task is canceled.

### Issue

1. Thread 1 calls [withTaskCancellationHandler(operation:onCancel:)](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/swift/withtaskcancellationhandler(handler:operation:)).
2. Thread 2 invokes [Task.cancel()](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/swift/task/cancel()), so the `onCancel` block runs immediately on Thread 2. ([`swift_task_cancelImpl`](https://github.com/swiftlang/swift/blob/main/stdlib/public/Concurrency/TaskStatus.cpp#L919))
3. At the same moment, the `operation` block executes on Thread 1.
4. Both threads access `var dataTask: URLSessionDataTask?` simultaneously.

### Fix

Access to dataTask is now guarded by a lock, guaranteeing the expected behavior even when cancellation happens concurrently.

author: lazy-rabbit-2001
body:
Closes: https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/12353
Also closes: https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/9575 in another way

Simply exposing `_edit_*` methods would bring with a lot of issues, so why not adding a node that achieves the similar way, with an interface exposed to users to customize their behavior of dragging the rect?

## Why not using `ReferenceRect`, as the latter is also used in 2D space
Even though it is, the new `HelperRect2D` is so light that it does take not so much space as `ReferenceRect`, and that users can easily customize their behavior by simply overriding `_rect_updated()`.

## What are the advantages of `HelperRect2D`?

- Lightness, as I've mentioned, this does not contain so many properties as `Control`-derived classes, i.e. the interface is neat and you will easily find the key properties of the node.
- Pureness, as this only provides a frame. Without any script, you can clip the children with this node, unlike `Sprite2D` which requires you to have its `texture` given so as to drag the border.
- Flexibility, as this is the nature of most of nodes in Godot. With a tool script, you can define your custom dragging behavior in the editor

author: raineorshine
body:
Fixes #2846.
Supersedes #2851.

- Converts `state.expandHoverDownPaths` from `Index<Path>` to `Path`. There's no need for multiple paths when only one path can be hovered over at a time.
- Replaces `state.expandHoverDownPath` with the new hovering path rather than adding to it.
- If hovering over a `SubthoughtDrop` zone, expands the `hoveringPath`. If hovering over a `ThoughtDrop` zone, then hoveringPath points to a sibling thought and we need to expand the parent.

author: hartig
body: This PR addresses #217 by extending the [definition of how to evaluate GRAPH patterns](https://www.w3.org/TR/sparql12-query/#defn_evalGraph) such that it now also considers blank nodes as possible graph names in an RDF dataset. Additionally, the PR: * changes the layout style of the changed definition such that it is consistent with the style of the other definitions in this part of the spec * removes the introduction of the notation _Ω_(_x_) from the beginning of Section [18.3 Basic Graph Patterns](https://www.w3.org/TR/sparql12-query/#BasicGraphPattern) * (this notation was used only in the definition that this PR changes and it was also not really clear; I have replaced it by something better directly in the changed definition now) * removes the notation _D_[_i_] from the beginning of Section [18.5.2 Evaluation Semantics](https://www.w3.org/TR/sparql12-query/#sparqlAlgebraEval) * (this notation was also used only in the definition that this PR changes) * removes the following paragraph which was placed directly below the changed definition but, in my opinion, doesn't really add anything (in fact, it is not even relevant because there can be no solution mapping that is in the result of more than one of the joins that feed into the union in the given algorithm)---but if you think it is useful to keep that paragraph, let me know and I will restore it! > The evaluation of graph uses the [Union](https://www.w3.org/TR/sparql12-query/#defn_algUnion) operator. The multiplicity of a solution mapping is the sum of the multiplicities of that solution mapping in each [Join](https://www.w3.org/TR/sparql12-query/#defn_algJoin) operation. *** Preview | Diff

author: atxtechbro
body:
## Description
This PR creates shared utility functions for MCP setup scripts to reduce code duplication and ensure consistent behavior across all setup scripts.

## Changes
- Created `mcp/utils/mcp-setup-utils.sh` with shared functions:
  - `check_docker_installed()` - Check if Docker is installed
  - `check_dotfiles_repo()` - Check if we're in the dotfiles repository
  - `get_repo_root()` - Get the repository root directory
  - `setup_mcp_servers_repo()` - Clone or update the MCP servers repository
  - `build_mcp_docker_image()` - Build Docker image for a specific MCP server
  - `update_secrets_template()` - Update .bash_secrets.example with API credentials template
  - `print_setup_complete()` - Print setup completion message
- Refactored all setup scripts to use the shared utilities
- Added documentation for the utility functions in `mcp/utils/README.md`
- Updated main README with information about the utility functions

## Benefits
- Reduced code duplication across setup scripts
- Easier maintenance - changes to common functionality only need to be made in one place
- Consistent behavior across all setup scripts
- Better documentation of the setup process
- Simplified setup scripts that are easier to read and understand

Closes #192

Release notes
Package name: @openzeppelin/contracts
  • 5.3.0 - 2025-04-09

    Breaking Changes

    • Replace GovernorCountingOverridable.VoteReceipt struct parameter member names hasOverriden and overridenWeight for hasOverridden and overriddenWeight respectively.

    Custom error changes

    • Replace GovernorAlreadyOverridenVote with GovernorAlreadyOverriddenVote.

    Changes by category

    Account

    • ERC4337Utils: Update the hash function to call getUserOpHash on the specified entrypoint and add an ENTRYPOINT_V08 constant. (#5614)
    • ERC7579Utils: Add ABI decoding checks on calldata bounds within decodeBatch. (#5371)
    • ERC7579Utils: Replace address(0) with address(this) during execution for calldata compression efficiency. (#5614)

author: casperlehmann
body:
The `JiraIssues.allowed_types` class variable is optional:

```python
class JiraIssues:
    _allowed_types: list[str] | None = None
```

We wan't it to stay nullable, in order to check for upstream issues when setting it. But we never actually want it to be `None`.

This PR forces a `ValueError` if the variable is about to be set to `None`. This allows us to remove fallbacks like this:
```python
assert 'Story' in (allowed_types or [])
```

body:
# Fix Instagram Scraper Timeout Issues

This PR addresses the timeout issues in scrape_reels.py when detecting Instagram Reels by updating selectors and extending timeouts.

## Changes

- Updated selectors to match the latest Instagram DOM structure
- Added multiple fallback selectors for Reels detection
- Implemented appropriate wait times before selector detection
- Extended wait_for_selector timeout to 60 seconds (60000ms)
- Added more detailed logging for troubleshooting
- Enhanced stealth mode with real Chrome browser integration
- Improved error handling for selector timeouts

## Technical Details

- Added multiple selector options for finding Reels links, videos, view counts, and profile information
- Implemented a selector fallback system that tries multiple selectors before failing
- Added wait for feed elements to appear before attempting to select Reels
- Enhanced logging to provide better visibility into the scraping process
- Used real Chrome browser with stealth mode to avoid Instagram's bot detection

These changes should resolve the "Timeout 30000ms exceeded" errors when scraping Instagram Reels.

Link to Devin run: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/ce35fc3e26a3409dbc746a0450740a17

## Description

This is a large PR with 55 files changed, but it's not as big as it looks!

Essentially, I've modified the structure of our Python structure so that `src` becomes the package that we import from. This way, we don't need to patch `PYTHONPATH` at all.

## Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Breaking change

## How Has This Been Tested?
To test this I:
- `cd`ed into the `data` directory
- set a `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` and `POSTGRES_PORT=5433` in an `.env` file
- spun up the Postgres database
- ran `pipenv run pytest`
- observed the tests passing

It establishes SSH connections to collect system metrics including CPU usage, memory utilization, disk space, network statistics, security metrics, and more. Comprehensive Metrics Collection: CPU, memory, disk, network, security metrics, and more Real-time Monitoring: Live system status checks and performance insights Multi-Server Support: Monitor multiple servers from a single MCP instance Threshold-based Alerts: Automatic detection of critical system conditions SSH Connection Management: Efficient connection pooling and reuse Security-focused: Monitor for failed login attempts, suspicious processes, and security updates MCP Integration: Ready for AI assistant interaction via the MCP protocol ## How Has This Been Tested? Tested directly with Claude Desktop ## Breaking Changes This is new feature ## Types of changes - [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) ## Checklist - [x] I have read the [MCP Protocol Documentation](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) - [x] My changes follows MCP security best practices - [x] I have updated the server's README accordingly - [x] I have tested this with an LLM client - [x] My code follows the repository's style guidelines - [x] New and existing tests pass locally - [x] I have added appropriate error handling - [x] I have documented all environment variables and configuration options ## Additional context The MCP server exposes the following tools: system_status: General system status information cpu_metrics: Detailed CPU metrics memory_metrics: Memory usage and swap statistics disk_metrics: Disk usage for all or specific mount points network_metrics: Network interface statistics security_metrics: Security-related metrics process_list: List of top CPU-consuming processes system_alerts: Current alerts based on threshold violations health_summary: Comprehensive health summary The system provides automatic alerts based on these default thresholds: CPU: Critical: Usage ≥ 90% Warning: Usage ≥ 80% Warning: Load average > 1.5 × core count Warning: I/O wait > 20% Memory: Critical: Usage ≥ 95% Warning: Usage ≥ 85% Warning: Swap usage ≥ 80% Warning: Free memory < 1GB (on systems with ≥ 2GB) Disk: Critical: Usage ≥ 95% Warning: Usage ≥ 85% Warning: Free space < 1GB (on disks ≥ 10GB) Warning: Inode usage ≥ 90% Warning: Disk I/O utilization > 80% Security: Warning: Failed logins > 10 Critical: Security updates > 5 Warning: Security updates ≥ 1 Warning: System not updated for ≥ 30 days Critical: Suspicious processes detected Warning: Unusual ports open

author: rawveg
body:
Design and implement a new feature for handling prompt parametrization within the application. This feature should enable the addition of parameters into a static prompt. These parameters should be easily identifiable and entered using a modal UI interface. The modal UI should allow for direct user input of parameter values, which will then populate the prompt dynamically when executed.

Upon execution with the specified parameters, the modal should trigger and facilitate the integration of the provided values into the static prompt dynamically during runtime. Ensure that the original prompt text in the UI remains unchanged post-execution. Furthermore, the feature should retain and remember previously entered parameter values for future executions, ensuring they are pre-populated in the modal to enhance user efficiency and experience.

Consideration should be given to the user interface design, ensuring it supports an intuitive and easy-to-use mechanism for parameter input, execution, and display without modifying the static prompt in the base user interface.

author: m-mburu
body:
add reusable function for facet-based performance metric visualization

This commit introduces the plot_facet_metrics function to visualize benchmarking or performance metrics across multiple test conditions using Seaborn’s relplot with facet grids. It is designed for flexibility and clarity in comparative analysis.

The function accepts a tidy or wide-format DataFrame, melts it into long format, and extracts key components from metric names — specifically the tree type (tst, bst) and test subtype (e.g., insert, search). These components are then used to organize the data across facets for more granular visual insights.

Key features:

Faceting: Metrics are split into subplots (facet_col, default: test_type) to help visually distinguish performance trends across different test types.

Hue support: Scenarios (or any other variable) can be color-coded for side-by-side comparison.

Optional confidence intervals: CI bands can be toggled off for uncluttered views or included for statistical variability.

Extensible preprocessing: Uses regex to parse column names assuming naming conventions like tst_insert, bst_search, etc., and assigns derived variables like tree and test_type.

This tool will be helpful for quickly comparing the performance of different algorithms or implementations across a range of input sizes or test configurations. It standardizes visualizations for benchmarking and supports further enhancements like styling, legends, or annotations if needed later.
